newsitem.title: POLAND: HSBC says Polish banking sector looks cheap.
newsitem.headline: HSBC says Polish banking sector looks cheap.

text.p: Polish banks on the Warsaw bourse look cheap after their recent underperformance and consumer and investment related stocks should provide good longer-term rewards, HSBC James Capel said in a report.
"The prospective market (1997) PE is around 10. The banking sector is cheap and is trading on a PE of just six times," the European Country Report dated August 1 said.
"Areas such as food, brewing and construction provide good potential while new issues will remain in strong demand," HSBC added, saying its favourite bank was BPH.

It said higher interest rates and the threat of further increases in reserves and possible credit restrictions had dampened enthusiasm for banks, but that the majority of such bad news had likely been discounted.

HSBC's year-end forecast for the all-share WIG index remained at 17,500, a nine-percent gain in dollar terms from the current level given HSBC's year-end exchange-rate forecast of 3.72 zlotys. The WIG closed at 15,116.8 points on Friday.
HSBC said strong 7.5-percent first-half GDP growth caused it to keep its six-percent 1997 GDP growth forecast for Poland despite recent flooding which should slow third-quarter growth.
